summary: The submission benchmarks cross-architecture representation transplantation between 14B and 32B language model layers using an answer-free scalar multiplier derived from median activation Euclidean distances. The benchmark evaluates 507 clean evaluation pairs against negative random controls and fitted interface baselines, demonstrating a 67.46 percentage point boost over raw unscaled edits. While technically sound and meticulously documented with hardware and software configurations, the scope remains restricted to single-digit assignment perturbations within a single model family.
strengths: Sound experimental design featuring an answer-free calibration set strictly isolated from the 512 held-out evaluation pairs
Inclusion of appropriate controls, including an equal-norm orthogonal random direction control that achieved zero reversals
Rigorous statistical reporting with exact paired counts and binomial confidence intervals
Precise documentation of execution environment, runtime (2m 44s), software versions (MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2), and CLI reproduction commands
weaknesses: The evaluation is confined to synthetic direct-return digit assignments and arithmetic operands, without testing broader semantic or multi-token edits
The specific base model checkpoints (e.g., Qwen 2.5 variants) are not explicitly named in the text, relying on external links and contextual inference
Lack of qualitative error analysis on the remaining 73 unreversed pairs to understand failure modes
suggestions: Explicitly name the foundation model family and specific checkpoint release identifiers directly in the text
Evaluate whether this scalar multiplier holds across diverse non-numeric token types and multi-step reasoning chains
Analyze the distribution and residual norms of the 73 failure pairs to characterize when scalar scaling fails

claims.text: A scalar of 2.625, measured from native assignment-state differences, raised the borrowed 14B interface from 92 to 434 full-vocabulary reversals in the frozen 32B receiver.
The gain improved on the raw direction by 67.46 percentage points [63.51, 71.60]. Its advantage over the previous norm match was 3.94 points [2.17, 5.92].
The Studio run took two minutes and 44 seconds using Python 3.12, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2 and NumPy 2.5.5 on the owner's Apple M5 Ultra.
claims.source: https://vdf.ai and notebookcheck.net (Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studio hardware and MLX framework specs)
